blocks.text: Duryodhana, on hearing Arjuna’s Pratijñā, consulted his advisors to come up with a plan to prevent Arjuna from killing Jayadratha in battle. Droṇācārya arranged a combination of three vyūhas (military formations) in order to protect Jayadratha from Arjuna. Bhīma, Sātyaki, and Arjuna tore through the Kaurava army but Jayadratha was hiding behind Droṇācārya, and it became very evident that Arjuna would not be able to kill Jayadratha before sunset. But Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa came to his rescue. Bhagavān sent his Sudarśanacakra to mask the sun and create the illusion of sunset. Jayadratha came out thinking the sun had set and that the Pratijñā had been forfeited. Bhagavān withdrew his Sudarśanachakra, revealing the sun. Seizing this opportunity Arjuna picked up his Gāṇḍīva and killed Jayadratha with the Pāśupatāstra.

Here we can see, Arjuna’s Pratijñā did not arise from clear thought. Rather it was an emotional response to the anger he felt, learning of his son’s death by adharma. Meanwhile, the Kauravas had planned well to defend Jayadratha from Arjuna and they would have succeeded if it was not for Bhagavān’s intervention.

Duryodhana, influenced by his uncle Śakuni, invited the Pāṇḍavas for a game of dice. Śakuni resorted to deceit, defeated Yudhiṣṭhira, and won his possessions one by one. Yudhiṣṭhira lost everything; his army, kingdom, his brothers, and himself to Duryodhana, and, finally even their wife
